MISSION STATEMENT
The City of Pasadena is
dedicated to delivering exemplary municipal services, responsive to our entire
community and consistent with our history, culture, and unique character.
In
compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, Assistive Listening Devices
are available at all City Council Meetings. Assistive Listening headphones and
neckloops can be checked out at the desk of the Sergeant-at-Arms, located inside
the City Council Chambers. To request meeting materials in alternative formats
or other disability-related modifications or accommodations necessary to
facilitate meeting participation, please contact the City Clerk’s Office as soon
as possible at (626) 744-4124 or
cityclerk@cityofpasadena.net .
Providing at least 72 hours advance notice will help ensure availability.
Language translation services are available for this meeting by calling
(626)744-4124 at least 24 hours in advance.
Habrá servicio de interpretación disponible para éstas juntas llamando al
(626)744-4124 por lo menos con 24 horas de anticipación .
Meetings are broadcast live on cable

https://www.cityofpasadena.net/city-manager/pasadena-media/
(Click on “Watch Now”)
Items on the agenda may not be called
in order listed. Agendas and
supporting documents are available on the Internet at
http://ww2.cityofpasadena.net/councilagendas/council_agenda.asp
Materials related to an item on this
Agenda submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency to the Pasadena Community
Development Commission after distribution of the agenda packet are
available for public inspection in the City Clerk’s Office at 100 N. Garfield
Avenue, Room S-228,
Pasadena, during normal business
hours.

CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  July 24, 2024-3:00 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL JOINT MEETING WITH
  LOS ANGELES COUNTY SUPERVISOR KATHRYN BARGER
OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called to order the special joint meeting with Los
  Angeles County Supervisor Kathryn Barger at 3:17 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Supervisor Barger.
ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Steve Madison
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton (absent)
  Councilmember Justin Jones (absent)
  Councilmember Jason Lyon
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  City Manager Miguel Marquez
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

  RECOGNITION AND APPRECIATION FOR CITY OF
  PASADENA AND COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES
  COLLABORATIVE EFFORTS RELATED TO THE H.O.U.S.E.
  PROGRAM, SENATE BILL 96 (HISTORIC VENUE
  RESTORATION AND RESILIENCY ACT), VARIOUS
  HOUSING PROGRAMS, AND UNITED MENTAL HEALTH
  PROMOTER SERVICES (UMHP) PROGRAM

  Dedan Brozino, Rose Bowl Chief Development Officer, provided
  an update on Senate Bill 96 relating to the Rose Bowl as a
  historic venue, and provided an oven/iew of how funds are
  reinvested into the venue for historic preservation, infrastructure
  improvements, technological retrofits, etc. He also spoke on
  legislative efforts at various levels of government to support and
  invest in historical venue infrastructure.

  Mateo Nix, founder of Homelessness Outreach Using Students
  in Education (H.O.U.S.E.), spoke on the H.O.U.S.E. internship
  program's curriculum and initiatives. The following students
  spoke on their experiences, presented outcomes and learnings
  from the H.O.U.S.E. internship, highlighted obstacles to
  overcoming homelessness, emphasized the importance of
  education and advocacy through community leadership, and

Council Minutes  1  07/24/2024
 r-  discussed affordable housing projects and issues: Mateo Nix,
  Mia Wertheimer, Mateo Gacina, Norah Kim, Lucas Truong.

  Jennifer O'Reilly Jones, Program Coordinator, presented
  information on various Housing Department collaborative
  projects with LA County, with the goal to address affordable
  housing and homelessness issues.

  Manuel Carmona, Acting Director of Public Health, spoke on the
  City's partnership with LA County to implement the United
  Mental Health Promoter Services Program, and reported on the
  program's initiatives to expand outreach and support for
  unhoused individuals.

  Adriana Bautista, Pasadena resident, expressed concerns
  regarding the Rose Bowl and encouraged community
  support for unhoused individuals.

  Following discussion, on the order of the Mayor, and consensus
  of the City Council, the information was received and filed.

  STATUS UPDATE ON CITY AND COUNTY
  COLLABORATION EFFORTS RELATED TO THE
  PROPOSED MIXED-USE DEVELOPMENT OF THE "KAISER"
  PROPERTY AT 434-470 NORTH LAKE AVENUE AND THE
  PROPOSED DEVELOPMENT OF THE RAMONA SENIOR
  HOUSING PROJECT AT 280 RAMONA STREET

  David Klug, Economic Development Director, provided an
  update on the Kaiser property and the disposition Surplus Lands
  Act process.

  Discussion ensued regarding the complexity of addressing
  homelessness, providing services for mental health and/or
  substance abuse issues and disorders, the implementation of
  the Supreme Court's Grants Pass decision, and working
  collaboratively to connect unhoused individuals, and individuals
  in need, with the essential services.

  Councilmember Rivas expressed enthusiasm for formalizing an
  agreement with LA County to establish mental health services
  and affordable housing at the Kaiser property.

  In response to Councilmember Williams' inquiry for an update on
  CARE Court, Lisa Wong, Director of Los Angeles County
  Department of Mental Health, briefly explained key initiatives of

  Council Minutes  2  07/24/2024
   CARE Court and discussed program details that CARE teams
  can use to assist individuals in making progress towards
  recovery. Director Wong also shared that County is working
  towards integrating substance use services with mental health
  to create a seamless system of care for clients.

  In response to Vice Mayor Madison's inquiry regarding potential
  collaboration on the Kaiser property, Joyce Chang, from Los
  Angeles County Chief Executive Office Real Estate Division,
  stated that LA County staff will work with City staff to identify
  ways where County services can be integrated on the property.

  Jim Wong, Senior Project Manager, provided an update on the
  Ramona Senior Housing Project, and briefly spoke on financial
  aspects and the developer's fundraising efforts for the affordable
  housing project.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that 6 letters in support of the
  Ramona Senior Housing Project and/or advocating for
  Supervisor Barger to approve funding to complete the project,
  were received by the City Clerk's Office, distributed to the City
  Council, posted online, and made part of the public record for
  the item.

  The following individuals spoke in support of the proposed
  Ramona Senior Housing Project and provided various
  comments pertaining to funding and necessity:

  Phil Hawkey, National Core
  Bert Newton, Making Housing and Community Happen
  Adriana Bautista, Pasadena resident
  Michael Canavan, Abundant Housing Pasadena

  Mayor Gordo expressed gratitude to Supervisor Barger and LA
  County staff for supporting and collaborating with the City to
  address the complex issues surrounding homelessness.

  On the order of the Mayor, and consensus of the City Council,
  the information was received and filed.
